column3: Hemispherical Position: India lies entirely in the Northern Hemisphere
Latitudinal Extent: Mainland extends from 8°4'N to 37°6'N
Tropic of Cancer: Divides India into almost two equal parts
Global Rank: Seventh largest country in the world
World Share: Accounts for 2.4 percent of world’s land area
Indian Standard Meridian: 82°30'E passing through Mirzapur
Time Logic: Avoids two-hour time lag between eastern and western India
Southern Neighbours: Sri Lanka and Maldives
Major Regions: Himalayas, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, Islands
Extent: Stretch 2,400 km from Indus to Brahmaputra

column4: Himadri: Northernmost and highest range with average height of 6,000 metres
Himachal: Rugged range south of Himadri with many hill stations
Shiwaliks: Outer range of unconsolidated sediments with duns

column3: Formation: Deposited by Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers

column4: Bhabar: Pebble belt along foothills
Terai: Marshy and swampy region
Bhangar: Older alluvium
Khadar: Newer and more fertile alluvium
Central Highlands: Region north of Narmada river
Deccan Plateau: Triangular landmass south of Narmada
Western Ghats: Higher, continuous, and closer to the coast
Eastern Ghats: Lower and discontinuous

column3: Location: Western margins of the Aravali Hills
Climate: Arid with very low rainfall
River: Luni is the only large river
Nature: Perennial rivers with year-round flow

column4: Indus: Originates near Lake Mansarowar in Tibet
Ganga: Formed at Devaprayag by Bhagirathi and Alaknanda
Brahmaputra: Known as Tsang Po in Tibet and Jamuna in Bangladesh
Narmada: Flows through rift valley into Arabian Sea
Tapi: Flows westward into Arabian Sea
Godavari: Largest peninsular river, also called Dakshin Ganga
Mahanadi: Flows into Bay of Bengal
Krishna: Major east-flowing river
Kaveri: Important river of southern India

column3: Wular Lake: Largest freshwater lake in India
Chilika Lake: Largest saltwater lake in India
Seasonal Winds: Climate marked by reversal of wind direction
Pressure and Winds: Affect monsoon system
Cold Weather Season: Mid-November to February
Hot Weather Season: March to May with hot dry loo winds
Advancing Monsoon: June to September with heavy rainfall
Retreating Monsoon: October to November with October heat
Tropical Evergreen Forests: Found in areas with rainfall above 200 cm
Tropical Deciduous Forests: Most widespread forests
Thorn Forests: Found in regions with rainfall below 70 cm
Montane Forests: Vegetation changes with altitude
Mangrove Forests: Found in tidal coastal regions
Delta Vegetation: Sundari trees in Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
Definition: Official population count every ten years
Determinants: Birth rate, death rate, and migration

column4: Internal Migration: Affects population distribution
International Migration: Affects population size and composition

column3: Education Goal: Free and compulsory education up to 14 years
